records.region: Central Virginia: selected upper Swift Creek and Swift Creek Reservoir through lower Swift Creek and the lower Appomattox to the James River junction at Hopewell.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named receiving-river system; different headward, waterbody and terminal component names remain bounded.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected connected Swift Creek–reservoir–lower Appomattox system. The upstream majority is separately labeled Swift Creek, including Swift Creek Reservoir; Appomattox River is not applied as a scalar name to those components. The selection reaches the James River confluence-side receiving setting and does not include the full natural Appomattox River.
records.completion_scope: All 15 stored parts, the reservoir entering/outlet connections, lower Swift-to-Appomattox join and separately considered source/render endings have ordinary geographic support in the inspected original map. The representative receiving-system result is complete; it does not claim uniform Appomattox naming of Swift Creek or of the reservoir.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected connected Swift Creek–reservoir–lower Appomattox system. The upstream majority is separately labeled Swift Creek, including Swift Creek Reservoir; Appomattox River is not applied as a scalar name to those components. The selection reaches the James River confluence-side receiving setting and does not include the full natural Appomattox River.

scope_limits: Appomattox River is a representative receiving-system candidate only; the map explicitly gives different names to the upstream Swift Creek and Swift Creek Reservoir components.
The chosen opening is not established as the natural source of Swift Creek or the Appomattox.
Generalized positions, cartographic scale and impounded/tidal water prevent exact channel-bank and hydronym-boundary claims.
Source and rendered endings differ slightly and represent an inland Appomattox–James receiving setting despite the stored sea classification.

records.region: Northern coastal Oregon: selected Nehalem River from an inland opening near the northeastern road-and-tributary valley through lower mountain bends, Nehalem Bay and its Pacific entrance.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named receiving-river system; different headward, waterbody and terminal component names remain bounded.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the selected connected Nehalem River and terminal bay/estuary system. The named river is followed throughout the inland selection; Nehalem Bay and the final ocean-entrance receiving setting are separate component scopes. This selection does not begin at the natural source of the full Nehalem River.
records.completion_scope: Both original mainstem fragments and all 24 stored parts have ordinary connected-river, floodplain and bay/entrance support in the inspected original map. The fragment seam and distinct coastal endings have been accounted for. No necessary receiving connection remains unresolved; the candidate remains representative rather than a blanket scalar river name for the bay.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected connected Nehalem River and terminal bay/estuary system. The named river is followed throughout the inland selection; Nehalem Bay and the final ocean-entrance receiving setting are separate component scopes. This selection does not begin at the natural source of the full Nehalem River.

scope_limits: The selected northeastern start is partway along the mapped river system, not a verified natural headwater.
Nehalem Bay and the Pacific entrance are terminal receiving components; uniform scalar river naming throughout them is not established.
Generalized route bends, cartographic scale and broad tidal plain limit exact channel, bank, slough and present-flow assignments.
The source and rendered endpoints differ within the bay-entrance coastal setting; neither is promoted to a surveyed mouth point or exact present shoreline.

records.region: Pacific-draining western Colombia: selected Naya river corridor from the La Concepción-side interior valley through forested alluvial lowlands and the lower coastal branch network.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative named receiving-river system; different headward, waterbody and terminal component names remain bounded.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the connected selected river and coastal receiving system, supported by photographic continuity and independent geographically located Naya references. This is not blanket naming of each modern lower branch or proof that the selected start is the river’s natural source.
records.completion_scope: Every stored part and both terminal definitions were compared against the original photographic view and overlapping native-resolution crops. Continuous ordinary valley, floodplain and estuarine correspondence is supported. Scattered clouds and generalized line positions prevent exact wet-thread claims but do not require an unresolved transfer between drainage systems. Naming remains representative, not formal registry acceptance.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected selected river and coastal receiving system, supported by photographic continuity and independent geographically located Naya references. This is not blanket naming of each modern lower branch or proof that the selected start is the river’s natural source.

scope_limits: Río Naya is a representative system candidate, not a formal registry decision or scalar label for every selected lower branch.

Cloud patches and model generalization limit exact present-channel/bank matching. Ordinary receiving corridors remain supported throughout.
The original and rendered endings occupy different points in the same estuarine island/channel transition; neither is promoted to a surveyed contemporary mouth.

records.region: Chihuahua, northward alluvial corridor and closed playa basin northeast of the state capital
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The successfully read imagery establishes the complete physical corridor but has no name labels. The optional Aldama–El Cuervo0816 technical-study notice failed before any source body was read. Discovery names, nearby place names and uninspected cartography do not establish the selected river or receiving-system identity.
records.geographic_disambiguation: All12 selected parts have complete ordinary geographic correspondence from an urban/agricultural opening through one northward desert alluvial floor into the northern playa. The inspected photographic source supplies no hydronym. This is a completed null-name scope hold; the optional naming-source pause is recorded separately.
records.completion_scope: Complete connected valley/alluvial-floor and playa correspondence, including all stored parts, joins and both separately preserved coincident terminal positions. No supported representative river-system name, accepted scalar name, Korean name, formal registry determination or application is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: The successfully read imagery establishes the complete physical corridor but has no name labels. The optional Aldama–El Cuervo0816 technical-study notice failed before any source body was read. Discovery names, nearby place names and uninspected cartography do not establish the selected river or receiving-system identity.

scope_limits: No supported hydronym is attached to any selected reach or the receiving playa in this finding. Search-discovery names are not substantive naming evidence.

The coarse selected line crosses built-up and cultivated portions of the same lowland and does not trace every present dark drainage mark. No current natural-versus-engineered channel condition or drainage operation is inferred.

A dry-looking alluvial/playa surface is sufficient for ordinary geographic correspondence. Perennial water, present flow, precise shorelines and a measured closed-basin water balance are not established.
The two terminal fields coincide but remain separately preserved. The endpoint was not shifted to a playa centre or present water edge.
Local imagery scene dates and formal naming-register status remain unverified.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
